content: Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can reduce the levels of baloxavir marboxil by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of bisacodyl, potentially leading to mucosal ulceration or ischemic colitis when stimulant laxatives are co-administered. This applies to both oral and rectal forms of bisacodyl. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can decrease the levels of demeclocycline, doxycycline, eravacycline, minocycline, omadacycline, sarecycline, and tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of these agents. To avoid chelation with magnesium, administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of polyethylene glycol/electrolytes and bisacodyl, potentially leading to mucosal ulceration or ischemic colitis. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can reduce the levels of raltegravir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of senna, potentially leading to mucosal ulceration or ischemic colitis. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of alendronate, aluminum hydroxide, amikacin, and amikacin liposome inhalation. Co-administration with medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of amiodarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may enhance the effects of amitriptyline, amoxapine, and other CNS depressants through an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely for evidence of seizures or enhanced CNS depression, especially when using higher doses of magnesium sulfate. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of amphotericin B (cholesteryl sulfate, deoxycholate, liposomal, and phospholipid complex formulations). Co-administration with medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of anagrelide by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may enhance the effects of aripiprazole and other CNS depressants through an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely for evidence of enhanced CNS depression. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of arsenic trioxide, asenapine, and asenapine transdermal by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of aspirin (oral, rectal, and combination formulations with citric acid and sodium bicarbonate). Co-administration with medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may enhance the effects of atracurium and other neuromuscular blocking agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of azilsartan, benazepril, betamethasone, bumetanide, candesartan, captopril, and other medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. This may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may reduce the levels of carbonyl iron by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of carboplatin, celecoxib, chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, and choline magnesium trisalicylate. Co-administration with medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may reduce the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may enhance the effects of cisatracurium and other neuromuscular blocking agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of cisplatin, citalopram, and other medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. This may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of clofazimine by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may enhance the effects of clomipramine, clozapine, and other CNS depressants through an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely for evidence of enhanced CNS depression. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of corticotropin, cortisone, cyclophosphamide, and other medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. This may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may reduce the levels of deferiprone by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer deferiprone at least 2 hours before and after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of deflazacort, dexamethasone, diclofenac, diflunisal, and other medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. This may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may reduce the levels of digoxin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer digoxin at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of disopyramide, dofetilide, and other medications by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may reduce the levels of dolutegravir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may enhance the effects of doxepin and other CNS depressants through an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely for evidence of enhanced CNS depression. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of dronedarone, droperidol, eliglustat, enalapril, eprosartan, and other medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. This may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may enhance the effects of escitalopram and other CNS depressants through an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely for evidence of enhanced CNS depression. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the toxicity of ethacrynic acid, ethanol, and etidronate. Co-administration with medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely.
